title: Let Not the Wise His Wisdom Boast
description: Let Not the Wise His Wisdom Boast in Tonic Solfa to SAVED BY GRACE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 422.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre Double (8.8.8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to SAVED BY GRACE; any other Long Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let not the wise his wis-dom boast, The might-y glo-ry in his might, The rich in flat-tering rich-es trust, Which take their ev-er-last-ing flight. The rush of nu-merous years bears down The most gi-gan-tic strength of man; And where is all his wis-dom gone, When dust he turns to dust a-gain?

lines: Let not the wise his wisdom boast,
The mighty glory in his might,
The rich in flattering riches trust,
The rush of numerous years bears down
The most gigantic strength of man;
And where is all his wisdom gone,
When dust he turns to dust again?
The boasting soul that knows his God;
When Jesus doth his blood apply,
I glory in his sprinkled blood.
The Lord my Righteousness I praise;
I triumph in the love divine,
The wisdom, wealth, and strength of grace,
In Christ to endless ages mine.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SAVED BY GRACE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
